brief.headline: Weeks of stock left across all families are {cover_total} against {cover_total_ly} last year; {top1_name} and {top2_name} have under {risk_threshold} weeks left, and {over1_name}, {over2_name} and {over3_name} have more than {overstock_threshold}.

items.text: Across all families there are {stock_total} units in stock, {stock_total_change} vs last year, and {cover_total} weeks of stock left against {cover_total_ly} last year.
Hero families have {hero_cover} weeks left against {hero_cover_ly} last year; Halo families have {halo_cover} against {halo_cover_ly}.

{top1_name} sells {top1_rate} units a week against {top1_rate_ly} last year and has {top1_stock} units in stock against {top1_stock_ly}; {top2_name} sells {top2_rate} against {top2_rate_ly} and has {top2_stock} against {top2_stock_ly}.

{over1_name}, {over2_name} and {over3_name} each have more than {overstock_threshold} weeks of stock; {over1_name} has {over1_cover} weeks against {over1_cover_ly} last year, and its sales are {over1_sales_yoy} vs last year.
{watch_name} is under the {overstock_threshold}-week threshold, with sales {watch_sales_yoy} vs last year and {watch_cover} weeks of stock left against {watch_cover_ly}.
Weeks of stock left fell from {top1_cover_prev} to {top1_cover} for {top1_name} and from {top2_cover_prev} to {top2_cover} for {top2_name}.
{most_over_name} fell from {most_over_cover_prev} to {most_over_cover} weeks. Families that changed stock status: {status_changes}.
The all-family figure is close to last year, while single families range from {top2_cover} weeks ({top2_name}) to {over1_cover} ({over1_name}).
{top1_name} and {top2_name}, the two families with the fewest weeks left, are also the top two by sales to first-time Gen Z customers ({genz_family1_diff} and {genz_family2_diff}).

Units sold per week rose most for {pace_up1_name}, from {pace_up1_prior} in weeks {pace_prior_first}–{pace_prior_last} to {pace_up1_latest} in weeks {pace_latest_first}–{pace_latest_last} (last year {pace_up1_prior_ly} and {pace_up1_latest_ly}); it has {pace_up1_cover} weeks of stock left. {pace_up2_name} went from {pace_up2_prior} to {pace_up2_latest}.

Units sold per week fell most for {pace_down1_name}, from {pace_down1_prior} to {pace_down1_latest} over the same weeks (last year {pace_down1_prior_ly} and {pace_down1_latest_ly}), and for {pace_down2_name}, from {pace_down2_prior} to {pace_down2_latest}.
Weeks of stock left divides units in stock at week {snapshot_week} by the average weekly units sold in weeks {rate_week_first} to {rate_week_last}, and assumes the coming weeks sell at that pace.

Weekly sales per family are small in this extract, about {units_per_week_total} units a week across all families, so a few orders move a family's weeks of stock left and its selling pace; the comparison with last year and the ranking between families are more reliable than the exact weeks.
Stock is one total for all stores and online, so this data cannot show stock by region or store, for example where Europe is {europe_yoy} and Greater China {china_yoy} vs last year.
There is no information on incoming orders or supplier lead times, so a family flagged as at risk of running out may already have stock on the way.

Season is not modelled: outerwear stock in August may include the fall delivery, and the {risk_threshold}- and {overstock_threshold}-week thresholds are placeholders to be set from lead times and the seasonal plan.
